content.text:
**Answers from the team notes**

1. Deleting a comment sets `deletedAt` to the time of deletion and keeps the row. Comments with a `deletedAt` value are left out of comment lists. Only the comment author may delete (policy-soft-delete.md).
2. Every new error response uses `{"error":{"code":"<machine_code>","message":"<text>"}}`. This replaces the older errors-by-field body. HTTP status codes do not change (policy-error-response.md).

**Source disagreement**

ops-runbook.md says new error responses should use the `errors` key shape. policy-error-response.md says new error responses use the error object. I followed policy-error-response.md. It is the rule written for new error responses and says it replaces the older body. The runbook has no date or version that would make it newer. code-error-shape.md describes what the code does today, so I used it only for the existing status values (422 for validation, 500 as the catch-all). The team should update the runbook, because support will not find the new error shape under the `errors` key.

**Checks**

| # | Rule (source) | Value in code (file:line) | Value from rule | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delete sets `deletedAt` and keeps the row (policy-soft-delete.md) | `deleteComment` uses `comment.update` with `deletedAt: new Date()` (article.service.ts:564-571) | set `deletedAt`, keep row | PASS |
| 2 | Deleted comments left out of lists (policy-soft-delete.md) | `getCommentsByArticle` has `where: { deletedAt: null }` (article.service.ts:442-446). No other comment list reads exist in the service. | excluded | PASS |
| 3 | Only the author may delete (policy-soft-delete.md) | Lookup filters `author.id: userId` and `deletedAt: null` (article.service.ts:536-541) | author only | PASS |
| 4 | `editedAt` is a nullable timestamp (policy-edited-at-marker.md) | `editedAt DateTime?` (schema.prisma, added in diff) | nullable | PASS |
| 5 | `editedAt` stays null until first edit, set to edit time on each successful edit (policy-edited-at-marker.md) | `editComment` writes `editedAt: now` (article.service.ts:580-640) | set on each edit | PASS |
| 6 | Migration must not change existing rows (policy-edited-at-marker.md) | `ADD COLUMN "editedAt" TIMESTAMP(3)`, no default, no update (20261030120000_comment_edited_at/migration.sql) | no row change | PASS |
| 7 | Edit allowed for 30 minutes after creation (policy-edit-window.md) | Refuses when `now - createdAt > 30 min` (article.service.ts:605). Exactly 30 minutes is allowed. | 30 minutes | PASS |
| 8 | Article list max 50, default 10 (policy-article-list-limit.md) | `take: Math.min(Number(query.limit) \|\| 10, 50)` (article.service.ts:85) | max 50, default 10 | PASS |
| 9 | Each new migration has a one-line undo note (policy-release-checklist.md) | Both migrations begin with `-- Undo: ...` | one line per migration | PASS |
| 10 | Migration folder named with a timestamp (code-migrations.md) | `20261030120000_...` and `20261030130000_...` | timestamped folders | PASS |
| 11 | Tests in `app/src/tests/services`, named `*.test.ts`, database mocked (code-test-layout.md) | three new or changed files, all use `prismaMock` | same | PASS |
| 12 | `npx prisma migrate deploy` run against a fresh database (policy-release-checklist.md) | Not run. I had no database here. | run before ship | NOT VERIFIED |
| 13 | Blank-body edit returns the new error object (policy-error-response.md) | `throw new HttpException(422, { errors: { body: ["can't be blank"] } })` (article.service.ts:582) | error object `{"error":{"code","message"}}` | **FLAG** |
| 14 | Edit refused when no comment of this user matches (policy-error-response.md) | `throw new HttpException(500, { errors: { comment: ['not found'] } })` (article.service.ts:600) | error object shape | **FLAG** |
| 15 | Edit refused after the window (policy-error-response.md, policy-edit-window.md) | `throw new HttpException(500, { errors: { comment: ['can no longer be edited'] } })` (article.service.ts:606-608) | error object shape | **FLAG** |

**Flag details**

- **Flag 13** (article.service.ts:582) breaks policy-error-response.md. The new error uses the errors-by-field body. The 422 status is unchanged, so it passes on status.
- **Flag 14** (article.service.ts:600) breaks policy-error-response.md on shape. The status is an open item. No note sets a status for a refused edit. The 500 comes from the code's own comment, which calls it the catch-all. code-comment-ownership.md gives 404 for "not found" on delete, but that is a different rule, so I did not apply it here. The team needs to choose a status.
- **Flag 15** (article.service.ts:606-608) has the same shape problem as Flag 14. Its status is the same open item.

**Notes, not flags**

- The 404 `{}` and 403 branches in `deleteComment` (article.service.ts:555, 559) are not new, and the diff does not change them, so I did not check them against the new shape rule. Per code-comment-ownership.md, the 403 branch cannot be reached.
- `article.service.test.ts` asserts the flagged 422 body, so the tests lock in the old shape. Changing the code will require changing that test.
- I did not run Jest or `prisma migrate deploy`. The results above come from reading the diff against the notes.

**Verdict: NOT APPROVED** (Flags 13, 14 and 15 against policy-error-response.md)
